title: Ship It: Deploy, Cost & Monitor

character.name: The Ops Ranger
character.tagline: A model in a notebook helps no one. Let's get it into the wild — and keep it alive.

oneLiner: The engineering around the model: serving via APIs, managing latency and cost, caching, and monitoring in production.
analogy: Training a model is baking a great cake at home; deploying it is opening a bakery that serves thousands daily without running out or going bankrupt. Now you care about: how fast each slice comes out (latency), how much each slice costs in ingredients (tokens = money), keeping popular slices pre-made (caching), and cameras in the kitchen (monitoring/observability) so you notice when quality drops or costs spike at 2am. The model is maybe 10% of the work; the bakery around it is the other 90%.
objectives: Serve models/LLMs behind APIs and understand latency vs cost tradeoffs.
Reduce cost with caching, smaller models, and prompt/token efficiency.
Monitor quality, latency, cost, and failures (observability) in production.
Understand streaming, rate limits, retries, and fallbacks for robust apps.
keyConcepts: LLM apps typically call a model API; you manage latency, throughput, rate limits, retries, and fallbacks around it.
Token usage drives cost: shorter prompts/outputs, smaller/cheaper models where adequate, and batching reduce spend.
Caching repeated or similar requests (and prompt caching) cuts both latency and cost.
Streaming tokens to the user improves perceived latency even when total time is unchanged.
Observability means logging inputs/outputs, latency, cost, and errors, plus tracking quality metrics and user feedback over time.
Right-size the model: use a smaller/cheaper model when it passes your evals, and reserve the biggest model for hard cases.

keyTerms.plain: How long the user waits for a response.
You pay per token in and out — words literally cost money.
Reusing past results so you don't pay/wait twice.
Showing the answer as it's typed, so it feels faster.
Cameras in the kitchen: logs and metrics for what your AI is doing.

scenarios.scenario: Your LLM app works but users complain it feels slow, even though total generation time is acceptable. Costs are also creeping up from repeated identical questions.
scenarios.question: Which two changes address these directly?

options.label: Stream tokens for perceived speed, and cache repeated requests to cut latency and cost
Switch to the largest model for everything

scenarios.explanation: Streaming improves perceived latency; caching repeated/similar requests reduces both latency and token cost. Bigger models and longer prompts would raise cost.

scenarios.scenario: A simple classification step in your pipeline currently uses your most expensive model and dominates the bill. It passes your evals easily.
scenarios.question: What's a sound cost optimization?

options.label: Right-size: use a smaller/cheaper model for that step since it already passes evals
Add more steps with the expensive model

scenarios.explanation: Match the model to the task: if a cheaper/smaller model passes your evals for a step, use it and reserve the expensive model for genuinely hard cases.

quiz.question: In LLM applications, what primarily drives cost?
quiz.explanation: You're billed per token processed, so prompt/output length and model choice directly affect cost.

quiz.question: Streaming tokens to the user primarily improves:
options: Perceived latency (it feels faster because output appears incrementally)
quiz.answer: Perceived latency (it feels faster because output appears incrementally)
quiz.explanation: Streaming shows text as it's produced, improving the felt responsiveness even when the total time is the same.

quiz.question: Caching in an LLM app helps by:
options: Reducing latency and cost for repeated or similar requests
quiz.answer: Reducing latency and cost for repeated or similar requests
quiz.explanation: Reusing prior results (and prompt caching) avoids recomputing the same work, saving time and money.

quiz.question: Observability for an AI system means:
options: Logging inputs/outputs, latency, cost, errors, and tracking quality over time
quiz.answer: Logging inputs/outputs, latency, cost, errors, and tracking quality over time
quiz.explanation: Observability lets you detect quality drops, cost spikes, and failures in production so you can respond quickly.

quiz.question: 'Right-sizing the model' means:
options: Choosing the smallest/cheapest model that still passes your evals for a given task
Shrinking the context window to zero
quiz.answer: Choosing the smallest/cheapest model that still passes your evals for a given task
quiz.explanation: Match the model to the difficulty of the task: use cheaper models where they suffice and reserve premium models for hard cases.
